results.text: [The role of metformin in the cardiokidney-metabolic patient]. Metformin is a first-line drug in the treatment of type2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) due to its efficacy, safety, and cost-effectiveness. Its main mechanism of action is the reduction of hepatic gluconeogenesis, improving insulin sensitivity and modulating glucose metabolism. Metformin enhances the action of insulin on porcine granulosa-lutein cells in vitro. Metformin is an oral antidiabetic drug extensively used to treat the polycystic ovary syndrome in women. Metformin increases insulin-stimulated glucose uptake and has direct effects on ovarian steroidogenesis in humans. However, the molecular mechanisms of metformin' action on the ovary are not clear.
